The CSP program aligns with numerous goals within Strategic priority 2: Enhance student achievement by cultivating an engaged and inclusive learning environment.
This is a unique program tied to a specific field of education.
The program is specifically dedicated to professional preparation in the field of College Student Personnel and does not overlap with any other programs at URI.

The Graduate Certificate in Community Planning (CP) is an online program that helps students develop core competencies in sustainable Community Planning.
Through this program, students will gain a foundation in the principles and practices of community planning and development, specifically in areas of land use and environmental planning.
The history of planning has many examples of environmental injustice, in which land use decisions have privileged some communities over others.
A commitment to anti-racism, inclusiveness, equity, as well as spatial and social justice perspectives is an integral part of a planning education.
Students can earn their certificate in four sessions, maximizing flexibility and convenience for career enhancement, leadership positions in the industry, and professional growth.
The Community Planning online certificate aligns with the University's commitment to urban initiative, community engagement and solving the world's most important challenges by equiping students with practical knowledge and understanding of how to plan for and enable equitable and sustainable communities.

This 4-course asychonous online graduate certificate also creates a learning opportunity for students who may not be able to attend graduate school in person on a full time basis, thereby creating a diverse learning opportunity (goal 3 of the URI Stragic Priority 2) and increase graduate student enrollment (goal 2 of Strategic Priority 2).
The impact of a working public better informed in values and strategies of community planning should contribute to healthier and more sustainable communities environmentally, socially and economically.
The online graduate Community Planning certificate will open doors for recent college graduates as well as working professionals; they will become eligible for positions and promotion in a growing job market.
By combining this online certificate with other stackable certificates such as Public Administration, MEM and GIS, students will be well equipped to engage in the significant planning challenges of our time.
Our department currently offers an in-person Graduate Certificate in Community Planning.
This proposed new program will be offered in the 7-week online format and require 4 classes with 3 required classes and one elective (12 credits).

Our existing Community Planning Graduate Certificate requires 5 courses to complete the certificate (15 or 16 credits).
The asychonous online certitificate is intended for a different student population from our in-person gradute certificate and provides somewhat different content.
The online certificate content is pragmatically planned to be useful for working professionals, adapted for online delivery, and geared towards working professionals who do not have prior knowledge of planning.
The purpose of the Certificate is to give these students a way to quickly and remotely attain a basic knowledge of planning, and to stack that knowledge with other certificates, such as Public Policy, Marine Affairs, GIS, etc.
By contrast, the full semester, in-person planning program encompasses a wide and in-depth disciplinary space, with opportunities to learn from in-person university relationships and pursue independent research, while still providing future planners with knowledge and tools for professional work.
